items.title: Edwin "Squirrel" Ashcraft Interview, 1961-08-16
items.q: I have to get back to Lix again because Lix were awful important.

ctx.x: Yes, it was what had been a small unit of the Speck band. And whether the whole Speck band was still playing or not, I don't know. I don't imagine they were.

Now, this was about seven, eight years after the New Orleans band, the original Lixie Lane Jazz band, had been in New York. Do you recall that anybody ever spoke about them as having introduced elements of jazz that they hadn't known before?

I think that everybody consciously knew that Nicola Rocca had had quite an influence on everything. I have to get back to Lix again because Lix were awful important. Yeah. And particularly in prescribed tunes where they weren't playing the lovely singing type tunes that Bix played. Also, Larry Shields, in his way, was the founder of a whole school of clarinet. And everybody imitated him. In his way, Emile Christian and Danny Edwards were the origin of tailgate trombone as far as any of us knew.
